set_title: Hydr- names: hydatid vs hydatidiform vs hydrops vs hydronephrosis vs hydrocephalus
stem: A 28-year-old woman at 10 weeks' gestation has vaginal bleeding and severe nausea. Uterine size matches 16 weeks, serum hCG is 280,000 mIU/mL and fetal heart tones are absent. Ultrasonography shows a heterogeneous mass with numerous small anechoic spaces.
oneliner: 28-year-old woman, 10 weeks, bleeding, uterus 16-week size, hCG very high → ?

whyNot.A: A liver parasitic lesion; she has **bleeding, a large uterus and very high hCG**
whyNot.B: Fetal edema with a living fetus; her **fetal heart tones are absent**
whyNot.C: Dilated kidney from obstruction; she has **uterine enlargement and high hCG**
whyNot.E: Gait, urinary and memory problems in elders; she has **bleeding and very high hCG**

why: Hydatid (watery drop) + -iform (shaped) + mole: a swollen, grape-like placenta. **Bleeding, large-for-dates uterus, hCG very high and cystic spaces** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Liver cyst with daughter cysts; sheep, dogs**

idea.rule: Hydatidiform = watery grape-like placenta; hydatid = parasite cyst; hydrops = fetal edema.
also: Snowstorm ultrasound; treat with suction curettage

set_title: Surgery endings: -ectomy (cut out), -otomy (cut into), -ostomy (opening), -plasty (repair), -pexy (fix in place), -lysis (break down)
stem: A 9-month-old boy has an empty right scrotum. A firm 1-cm testis is palpable in the inguinal canal and cannot be moved into the scrotum. Which procedure is indicated, ideally by 18 months?
oneliner: 9-month-old boy, empty scrotum, testis in the canal → which procedure?
ask: Which term names the indicated procedure?

whyNot.A: Removes the gallbladder; his problem is an **undescended testis**
whyNot.B: Cuts pyloric muscle; his problem is an **empty scrotum with a canal testis**
whyNot.D: Opens the airway; his problem is an **undescended testis**
whyNot.E: Breaks down a clot; his problem is a **testis stuck in the canal**

why: Orchio- (testis) + -pexy (fix in place): surgically fixing the testis in the scrotum. **An undescended testis stuck in the inguinal canal** needs it.

idea.rule: -pexy fixes in place; -ectomy removes; -otomy cuts into.
also: Cryptorchidism raises germ cell tumor risk

set_title: Endometri- names: endometriosis vs endometritis vs adenomyosis vs leiomyoma
stem: A 30-year-old nulligravid woman has pelvic pain that begins before and peaks during menses, pain with intercourse and 2 years of infertility. Examination shows a fixed retroverted uterus and nodules along the uterosacral ligaments. Ultrasonography shows a 4-cm ovarian cyst with ground-glass echoes.
oneliner: 30-year-old woman, cyclic pelvic pain, dyspareunia, infertility, chocolate ovarian cyst → ?

whyNot.B: Causes postpartum fever and tenderness; she has **cyclic pain and a chocolate cyst**
whyNot.C: Gives a soft globular uterus; hers is **fixed and retroverted with an ovarian cyst**
whyNot.D: Gives a firm irregular uterus; she has **uterosacral nodules and a chocolate cyst**
whyNot.E: Causes abnormal bleeding with unopposed estrogen; she has **cyclic pain and infertility**

why: Endometrium + -osis (abnormal condition): endometrial tissue outside the uterus. **Cyclic pain, dyspareunia, infertility and a chocolate cyst** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Cyclic pelvic pain, dyspareunia, infertility; chocolate cyst**

idea.rule: Endometriosis = tissue outside the uterus; adenomyosis = tissue inside the myometrium.

set_title: Endometri- names: endometriosis vs endometritis vs adenomyosis vs leiomyoma
stem: A 28-year-old woman has a temperature of 38.9 C and lower abdominal pain 3 days after an emergency cesarean delivery following prolonged labor. The uterus is tender and soft with foul-smelling lochia. Leukocyte count is 17,000/mm3.
oneliner: 28-year-old woman, fever 3 days after cesarean, tender uterus, foul lochia → ?

whyNot.A: Causes cyclic pain and infertility; she has **fever after cesarean with foul lochia**
whyNot.B: Causes chronic heavy painful menses; she has **acute fever and foul lochia**
whyNot.C: Gives a firm, nontender, irregular uterus; hers is **tender and soft with fever**
whyNot.E: Presents with postmenopausal bleeding; she has **fever 3 days after cesarean**

why: Endometrium + -itis (inflammation): infection of the uterine lining. **Fever, tender uterus and foul lochia after cesarean delivery** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Cyclic pelvic pain, dyspareunia, infertility; chocolate cyst**

idea.rule: -itis = infection or inflammation; -osis = abnormal condition. Postpartum fever plus tender uterus.
also: Polymicrobial; treat with clindamycin plus gentamicin
Cesarean and prolonged labor are risks

set_title: Endometri- names: endometriosis vs endometritis vs adenomyosis vs leiomyoma
stem: A 45-year-old multiparous woman has 2 years of heavy, increasingly painful menses. The uterus is uniformly enlarged, soft, globular and tender at 12-week size. A pregnancy test is negative and MRI shows a thickened junctional zone.
oneliner: 45-year-old multiparous woman, heavy painful periods, soft globular uterus → ?

whyNot.A: Gives a fixed retroverted uterus with cyst; hers is **soft, globular and uniformly enlarged**
whyNot.C: Causes fever after delivery or procedures; she has **chronic heavy painful menses**
whyNot.D: Gives a firm, irregular uterus; hers is **soft, globular and uniform**
whyNot.E: Causes painless abnormal bleeding; she has **painful menses and a tender globular uterus**

why: Adeno- (gland) + myo- (muscle) + -osis: endometrial glands within the myometrium. **Painful heavy menses and a soft globular uterus** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Cyclic pelvic pain, dyspareunia, infertility; chocolate cyst**

idea.rule: Adenomyosis = glands inside the uterine muscle; soft, uniform, globular uterus.
also: Older multiparous women; pain with menses

set_title: Endometri- names: endometriosis vs endometritis vs adenomyosis vs leiomyoma
stem: A 38-year-old Black woman has had heavy menses with clots for 1 year and urinary frequency. Examination shows a firm, nontender, irregularly enlarged uterus at 14-week size. Hemoglobin is 9 g/dL.
oneliner: 38-year-old Black woman, heavy periods, firm irregular nontender uterus → ?

whyNot.A: Gives cyclic pain and a fixed uterus; hers is **firm, irregular and painless**
whyNot.B: Causes fever and a tender uterus; hers is **nontender and chronic**
whyNot.C: Gives a soft, globular, tender uterus; hers is **firm and irregular**
whyNot.D: Presents with postmenopausal bleeding; she is **38 with a firm irregular uterus**

why: Leio- (smooth) + myo- (muscle) + -oma (tumor): a benign smooth muscle tumor. **Heavy bleeding with a firm, irregularly enlarged uterus** in a Black woman fits.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Cyclic pelvic pain, dyspareunia, infertility; chocolate cyst**

idea.rule: Fibroid = firm irregular uterus; adenomyosis = soft globular uterus.
also: Leiomyosarcoma arises de novo, not from fibroids

set_title: -ectasia words: something widened (telangiectasia, duct ectasia, lymphangiectasia)
stem: A 48-year-old woman who breastfed three children has a thick green-black discharge from the left nipple. The nipple is slightly retracted and tender beneath, with no discrete mass.
oneliner: 48-year-old woman, multiparous, thick green-black nipple discharge + retracted tender nipple → ?

whyNot.B: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia causes nosebleeds; she has a **thick green-black nipple discharge**
whyNot.C: Ataxia-telangiectasia is a childhood immune and cerebellar disease; she is **48 with nipple discharge**
whyNot.D: Intestinal lymphangiectasia is a gut disease; her complaint is a **nipple discharge**
whyNot.E: Bronchiectasis is a lung disease; she has **breast and nipple findings**

why: Mammary (breast) + duct + ectasia (widening): dilated subareolar ducts with inflammation. **Thick green-black nipple discharge in a multiparous older woman** is duct ectasia.

idea.rule: Ectasia = widening; mammary duct ectasia widens breast ducts.

set_title: Paget names: bone remodeling vs breast and skin cancer (and an effort clot)
stem: A 60-year-old woman has had a scaly, crusted, eczema-like rash on the right nipple for 6 months that did not heal with steroid cream. Biopsy shows large cells with clear halos within the epidermis. Mammography shows an underlying mass.
oneliner: 60-year-old woman, 6-month scaly crusted nipple, steroid-resistant + large clear-halo cells in epidermis + underlying mass → ?

whyNot.A: Paget disease of bone raises ALP; she has a **nipple rash**
whyNot.B: Extramammary Paget disease is outside the breast; hers is a **nipple lesion**
whyNot.D: Paget-Schroetter is a vein clot of the arm; she has a **crusted nipple**
whyNot.E: Pagetoid reticulosis is limb T-cell lymphoma; she has a **nipple lesion with a mass**

why: Malignant ductal cells spread up into the nipple epidermis. **A steroid-resistant scaly nipple, large clear-halo cells and an underlying mass** mean ductal carcinoma.

idea.rule: Paget of the breast: nipple eczema that never heals means underlying cancer.
also: Usually underlying DCIS or invasive cancer

set_title: Myelo- names: marrow or spinal cord?
stem: A 1-day-old girl is born with a soft sac over her lower back that is covered by a thin membrane and contains neural tissue. She does not move her legs, and her anal tone is reduced. Her mother took valproic acid for epilepsy during pregnancy, and her mother's serum alpha-fetoprotein was high at 16 weeks.
oneliner: Newborn girl + lumbosacral sac containing neural tissue + leg paralysis + valproate in pregnancy, high maternal AFP → ?

whyNot.B: Myelophthisis is tumor-filled marrow in adults; she is **a newborn with a back sac**
whyNot.C: Transverse myelitis develops over days, often post-infection; her deficit is **present at birth**
whyNot.D: Myelodysplastic syndrome affects marrow in older adults; she has **a congenital back sac**
whyNot.E: Myelofibrosis scars marrow in older adults; she has **a neural-tissue sac at birth**

why: Spinal cord + meninges + sac: they bulge through an open vertebral arch. **Newborn back sac with neural tissue, weak legs, high AFP, valproate** means myelomeningocele.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Sensory level on trunk with bladder trouble**

idea.rule: Myelo- = spinal cord in myelomeningocele and myelitis; marrow in the rest.
also: Chiari II and hydrocephalus go with it
Folic acid before conception prevents it
